claims: CSR supports direct (data, indices, indptr) construction; canonical rows have sorted indices and no duplicates; nnz includes explicit zeros.
LIL uses Python row/data lists, can incur linear insertion per item, and its insert implementation deletes x == 0 entries.
Radau converts sparse callable Jacobians to CSC and selects splu; it does not necessarily run dense LU.
source_records.application: Replace only Python insertion/format work while preserving FD calls, numeric values, sorted column order and zero pattern.
limitations: Documentation version is an explicit reviewed reference, not a claim about the installed runtime.
Keeping explicit structural zeros can change downstream symbolic ordering despite mathematical equality.

claims: Partial pairwise summation depends on axis and memory layout; exact precision also depends on other parameters.
source_records.application: Do not use algebraic equivalence alone to claim bitwise equality after transpose, dot/einsum, SIMD or layout changes.
limitations: No blanket claim that all NumPy sums are pairwise or that all dot operations match CSR order.

claims: CVodeSetJacTimes registers optional setup and Jacobian-vector callbacks with user data.
CVODE separates saved Jacobian data from the step-coefficient-dependent linear matrix I-gamma*J.
source_records.application: Separate immutable structure, exact-state numeric blocks, and (Jacobian identity, stage coefficient) factors.
limitations: Use is design precedent only; no CVODE adoption or new approximate Jacobian-reuse schedule.
The main-branch source is supporting text; the versioned documentation is the stable API reference.

claims: PartialPivLu::new accepts a matrix view and exposes L, U and P.
Solve::solve_in_place writes the solution into the RHS buffer.
The lower-level LU solve API accepts Par and explicit MemStack scratch.
Par::Seq is sequential but the documentation does not promise cross-platform bitwise portability; Rayon uses a thread pool.
source_records.application: Reuse the already selected faer version for only the 4x4 gas Schur factor/solve if root wires a compatible optional backend.
limitations: High-level in-place does not promise zero internal allocation; factor/scratch ownership must be measured.
Existing default-features=false std/linalg/sparse-linalg selection should not be replaced with faer defaults, which include rayon/rand/npy.
Sequential mode is not a no-FMA or cross-CPU bitwise guarantee; validate residual and physical acceptance separately.
No dense n x n reconstruction on the hot path.

claims: ThreadPoolBuilder::num_threads and build configure a pool; ThreadPool::install runs parallel operations within it.
par_chunks_mut gives nonoverlapping mutable output chunks.
Floating-point sum/reduce order is not specified; results need not be deterministic.
source_records.application: Conditional only: independent output rows/chunks with unchanged serial inner reduction. No dependency addition unless measured benefit.
limitations: K 512-896 and eleven long reduction rows do not justify a 64-thread expectation.
Do not use floating par_iter().sum/reduce, build a pool per callback, or multiply Rayon x faer x BLAS/MPI thread counts.
No parallel callback into the opaque physical owner unless its ownership/thread safety is independently established.

source_records.title: Using SIMD and SIMT vectorization to evaluate sparse chemical kinetic Jacobian matrices and thermochemical source terms
claims: The paper studies source/Jacobian vectorization and data ordering using sparse/dense chemical kinetic Jacobians.
source_records.application: Supports profiling Jacobian evaluation and layout independently from integration.
limitations: HE29 has a fixed opaque thermochemical owner; pyJac chemistry reformulation and its reported speedups are not transferred.
SciSpace indexed date was not used as publication date.

source_records.title: Accelerating finite-rate chemical kinetics with coprocessors: comparing vectorization methods on GPUs, MICs, and CPUs
claims: The paper compares SIMD/SIMT RHS and stiff/nonstiff solver work and analyzes divergence due to adaptive step sizes.
source_records.application: Separate per-state vectorization from parallel execution of distinct adaptive solves.
limitations: Hardware, kinetic models and many-IVP workload differ from four HE29 reference pairs; no speedup number is adopted.

source_records.title: Self-Consistent Solution of Cosmological Radiation-Hydrodynamics and Chemical Ionization
claims: A fully implicit inexact Newton radiation/ionization/gas system uses a Schur formulation to separate local microphysics from radiation transport, then multigrid-preconditioned CG for its diffusion Schur system.
source_records.application: Context for exploiting the actual coupled Jacobian structure, not a copied solver.
limitations: The paper uses spatial FLD/PDE transport; HE29's local finite-donor diagonal photon block yields a different 4x4 gas Schur problem.
No CG/SPD or global EoR/scalability conclusion follows for HE29.

scispace_queries: Which primary research papers measure sparse analytic Jacobian or Jacobian-vector-product acceleration for stiff chemical-kinetics ODEs, and what do they show about avoiding sparse matrix assembly, preserving reaction-rate arithmetic, and the limits of parallel speedup for small systems?

Which primary numerical-method papers use Schur-complement elimination or block preconditioning for radiation-matter or thermochemical coupling where many radiation variables interact with only a few material variables, and what are their memory-cost and Jacobian-reuse assumptions?
